articles.content:
BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM

Eight months after a shooting at a Hanukkah celebration in Bondi Beach killed 15 people, Australia is following through. New South Wales starts a gun buyback on November 2, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese confirmed Sunday. It’s the largest the country has run since Port Arthur.

What the buyback looks like

People returning rifles and handguns get up to A$1,000 (around $700) per firearm. Albanese and New South Wales Premier Chris Minns announced it together, with both federal and state governments behind it.

It’s part of a January package that also included tighter gun licence checks and a crackdown on hate. New South Wales added its own cap: individuals can now legally own a maximum of four guns under state law.

Why the numbers matter

Australia hit a record 4.1 million registered firearms last year, more than 1.1 million of them in New South Wales. The firearms used in the December attack were legally obtained, which is part of why the political response moved as fast as it did. “Australians are quite rightly proud of our gun laws,” Albanese said in televised remarks, “but the fact is there are more guns in Australia today than there were at the time of dealing with the Port Arthur gun buyback.”

Police say the attack was carried out by a father and son they believe were inspired by Islamic State. The surviving suspect, Naveed Akram, 24, hasn’t entered pleas yet on charges that include 15 counts of murder.

The Port Arthur comparison

The 1996 Port Arthur massacre in Tasmania killed 35 people. The buyback that followed removed roughly 650,000 firearms and is credited with a sustained drop in mass shootings afterward. Whether this one gets there depends on how many people participate, which won’t be clear for months. November 2 is the start date.

articles.personality_title: Australia launches biggest gun buyback in 30 years to reduce violence
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Australia is responding to a tragic shooting that happened eight months ago at a Hanukkah celebration in Bondi Beach, where 15 people lost their lives. The country has a history of strong gun laws, especially after a major reform following the Port Arthur massacre in 1996.

**What happened** – On November 2, New South Wales (NSW) will begin the largest gun buyback program since 1996. People can return rifles and handguns in exchange for up to A$1,000 (about $700) per gun. This effort is supported by both the federal government, led by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and the NSW state government.

**Impact** – This buyback aims to reduce the number of guns in Australia, especially in NSW, which has over 1.1 million registered firearms. The recent attack used legally owned guns, pushing the government to act quickly. The program also introduces a legal limit of four guns per person in NSW, along with stricter licensing and measures against hate crimes. The 1996 Port Arthur buyback removed around 650,000 guns and helped lower mass shootings for years. This new buyback hopes to achieve similar results.

**What’s next step** – The success of the buyback will depend on how many people choose to return their guns. It will take months to see the full impact. The government will continue to enforce tighter gun rules and monitor safety to prevent future violence.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Australia’s largest gun buyback in three decades starts this November, aiming to reduce gun violence by buying back firearms and tightening ownership rules.
articles.personality_title_fr: L'Australie lance le plus grand rachat d'armes depuis 30 ans pour réduire la violence
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – L'Australie réagit à une fusillade tragique survenue il y a huit mois lors d'une célébration de Hanoukka à Bondi Beach, où 15 personnes ont perdu la vie. Le pays a une longue histoire de lois strictes sur les armes, notamment après une réforme majeure suite au massacre de Port Arthur en 1996.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Le 2 novembre, la Nouvelle-Galles du Sud (NSW) commencera le plus grand programme de rachat d'armes depuis 1996. Les personnes peuvent rendre leurs fusils et pistolets en échange d'un maximum de 1 000 dollars australiens (environ 700 $) par arme. Cette initiative est soutenue à la fois par le gouvernement fédéral, dirigé par le Premier ministre Anthony Albanese, et le gouvernement de l'État de NSW.

**Impact** – Ce rachat vise à réduire le nombre d'armes en Australie, en particulier en NSW, qui compte plus de 1,1 million d'armes enregistrées. L'attaque récente a utilisé des armes légalement détenues, ce qui a poussé le gouvernement à agir rapidement. Le programme impose aussi une limite légale de quatre armes par personne en NSW, ainsi que des contrôles plus stricts sur les licences et des mesures contre les crimes haineux. Le rachat de Port Arthur en 1996 avait retiré environ 650 000 armes et aidé à réduire les fusillades de masse pendant des années. Ce nouveau rachat espère obtenir des résultats similaires.

**Prochaine étape** – Le succès du rachat dépendra du nombre de personnes qui choisiront de rendre leurs armes. Il faudra plusieurs mois pour mesurer l’impact complet. Le gouvernement continuera à appliquer des règles plus strictes et à surveiller la sécurité pour prévenir de nouvelles violences.

**En une phrase** – Le plus grand rachat d'armes en Australie depuis trois décennies commence en novembre, visant à réduire la violence par le rachat d'armes et le renforcement des règles de possession.
articles.personality_title_es: Australia inicia la mayor recompra de armas en 30 años para reducir la violencia
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Australia está respondiendo a un tiroteo trágico ocurrido hace ocho meses en una celebración de Janucá en Bondi Beach, donde 15 personas murieron. El país tiene una historia de leyes estrictas sobre armas, especialmente después de una reforma importante tras la masacre de Port Arthur en 1996.

**Qué pasó** – El 2 de noviembre, Nueva Gales del Sur (NSW) comenzará el programa de recompra de armas más grande desde 1996. Las personas pueden devolver rifles y pistolas a cambio de hasta 1.000 dólares australianos (unos 700 dólares estadounidenses) por arma. Esta iniciativa cuenta con el apoyo del gobierno federal, dirigido por el primer ministro Anthony Albanese, y del gobierno estatal de NSW.

**Impacto** – Esta recompra busca reducir la cantidad de armas en Australia, especialmente en NSW, que tiene más de 1,1 millones de armas registradas. El reciente ataque usó armas legalmente obtenidas, lo que llevó al gobierno a actuar rápidamente. El programa también establece un límite legal de cuatro armas por persona en NSW, junto con controles más estrictos de licencias y medidas contra los crímenes de odio. La recompra de Port Arthur en 1996 retiró alrededor de 650,000 armas y ayudó a disminuir los tiroteos masivos durante años. Esta nueva recompra espera lograr resultados similares.

**Qué sigue** – El éxito dependerá de cuántas personas decidan entregar sus armas. Tomará meses ver el impacto completo. El gobierno seguirá aplicando reglas más estrictas y vigilando la seguridad para prevenir futuras violencias.

**Resumen en una frase** – La mayor recompra de armas en Australia en tres décadas comienza en noviembre, con el objetivo de reducir la violencia mediante la devolución de armas y el endurecimiento de las leyes de posesión.
